quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What does smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle do?

options.text: It serves no purpose.
It lets the engine help slow down the motorcycle.
It is against the law.
You should not do it when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets the engine help slow down the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through smooth downshifting is helpful for riders. If you use engine braking, turn on your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medicines usually affect you?

options.text: They make you sleepy.
They make you more awake.
They make you hungry.
They make it hard to focus.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medicines for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety cause drowsiness and can hurt your ability to ride safely. Before riding, learn how any medicine you take affects your body.

questions.question: What does a shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It protects your face if you crash.
It only protects you from dirt.
It does not protect as well as goggles.
You should not wear it with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects your face if you crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield also shields you from dirt, dust, bugs, rain, and rocks.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels may slip and lose grip.
You stop sooner than expected.
Your tire pops.
It takes longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels may slip and lose grip.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause your wheels to lose grip. This can result in a crash.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, what following distance should you keep?

options.text: At least four seconds behind the other vehicle.
Get as close as you can to the other vehicle.
Do not worry about how far back you are.
Always ride on the left side of your lane so drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least four seconds behind the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance between them and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should proper motorcycle riding clothing cover?

options.text: Your arms and legs completely.
Your arms completely, but not your legs.
Your legs completely, but not your arms.
Whatever feels most comfortable, safety does not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: For safety while riding, wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to let them pass.
Speed up to put distance between you.
Ignore them.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may make things worse by encouraging them to follow faster.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you stay out of blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
Help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, and gives you an escape route. Your position should make you visible to other drivers, not hide you.

questions.question: What can a motorcycle horn do?

options.text: It serves no purpose.
Other drivers cannot usually hear it.
It can get someone's attention quickly.
You should never use it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can help get someone's attention fast. However, motorcycle horns are not as loud as car horns, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid danger.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and wait for the dog to lose interest.
Swerve around the dog.
Slow down toward the dog, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down toward the dog, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog is chasing you, slow down and approach it calmly. Once you are close, speed up and leave it behind. Do not kick the dog.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, you should:

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Only ride in the afternoon.
Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Tell other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle. Always look ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Handles curves the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be operated in curves.
Should use the shoulder when taking a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Handles curves differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders with less than six months of riding experience.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of riding experience.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time for a quick stop.

questions.question: An advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles is:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrower view so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can more easily follow the next vehicle's path.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: If a driver makes eye contact with you:

options.text: It means they see you.
It will never happen.
It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
It guarantees they will yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee they will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not trust eye contact. Drivers may look directly at you but not actually see you. They may fail to yield to you.

questions.question: What color are warning signs with black lettering?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, it is usually best to:

options.text: Relax on the handgrips.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold both handgrips firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake to the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that go above the ankle
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection.
